title: ci: bump validate runner and machine timeout
body:
With the CNCF downgrade machine tests take an hour, a larger runner
also does not really speed this up so just bump the timeout there.

Also upgrade the validate task as golangci-lint is quite slow otherwise
and this blocks until the real tests start so we like to have this down
quicker.

comments.body:
> 57m 23s 

Does not seem to gain us much, 2 minutes maybe but I guess that is a bit better at least?

For validate it does seem a few minutes faster which is a lot more important there as it blocks until the real tests start so I guess it worth to merge this for now at least until the CNCF regressions are fully understood.

hey Pual, I pulled the machine job history now and takes around 38 min on the old runners, and since the swap 43 and 58.6 finishing plus one killed at 60.3, so there is no upper bound on that one i think... and the slowdown also looks about the same on every shape I could compare, **39 percent on 4cpu** and **43 on 8cpu**, though only one job each on the bigger shapes so that part is thin for now

> For validate it does seem a few minutes faster which is a lot more important there as it blocks until the real tests start so I guess it worth to merge this for now at least until the CNCF regressions are fully understood.

I think it makes sense. validate took one of the bigger hits anyway, about 5.8 to 9.5 min across the swap, so a few minutes back is most of it as of now.
@Luap99 Is it worth bumping to a double-size instance if it buys us this little? Seems a little wasteful

> @Luap99 Is it worth bumping to a double-size instance if it buys us this little? Seems a little wasteful

The validate one is needed for sure IMO, the machine one we can drop.
